parts.text: "Use only the python tool. In one Python program: a = fs.read(\"vision.png\"); b = web.fetch(\"http://127.0.0.1:8000/vision.png\"); return {\"read\": a, \"fetch\": b}. Do not use browser. After the tool result, tell me the exact text visible in the images."

The user wants me to run a Python program that reads vision.png from the filesystem and fetches it from localhost:8000. Then report exact text visible in the images. But fs.read returns text — a PNG would be binary. Let me just do it as asked and see.

Let me write the program as instructed.

Both images show "VISION-OK-739". Report exact text.

Note the caveat: the read tool returned only path/mime metadata, but the image was rendered (attached). Both images show same text. I should be accurate: fs.read didn't return text content, it returned metadata, but the image was rendered as attached media. The web.fetch returned "Image fetched successfully" plus the rendered image.

Report exact text.

Both images show the same text:

**`VISION-OK-739`**

Details of what each returned:

- **`fs.read("vision.png")`** — returned metadata only: `path: "vision.png"`, `mime: "image/png"` (no text field). The image itself rendered as the first attachment, showing the white text `VISION-OK-739` on a dark navy rectangle in the upper-left of a white background.
- **`web.fetch("http://127.0.0.1:8000/vision.png")`** — returned `mime: "image/png"`, `text: "Image fetched successfully"`, `title: "... (image/png)"`. The rendered image (second attachment) is visually identical, showing `VISION-OK-739`.

So the only readable text in the image content is `VISION-OK-739`; the string "Image fetched successfully" is the fetch tool's status message, not text inside the image.
